rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis varies Al content to promote γ′ (L12) precipitates in an FCC matrix, whereas the paper annealed a fixed-composition alloy at different temperatures to study BCC/B2 phase formation. This is a different kind of intervention.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis uses aging at ~800°C and tests under radiation/cryogenic conditions, while the paper annealed at 1100–1300°C under Ar and water-quenched, measuring hardness at room temperature. The regimes are different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis proposes Al-driven γ′ precipitation hindering diffusion and enhancing twinning, whereas the paper describes spinodal decomposition and ordering into BCC/B2 phases driven by Ni–Al partitioning. These are different mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved high-temperature strength, oxidation/radiation resistance, and cryogenic toughness via γ′ precipitates, while the paper reports increased hardness with higher annealing temperature due to BCC/B2 microstructures. The predicted properties and direction differ.
